## Philosophy: Retrospective vs. Predictive

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Predictive Systems (SP+, FPI)
- **Objective:** Forecast who wins tomorrow on a neutral field.
- **Weights:** Margin of victory, play efficiency, recruiting rankings.
- **Penalty:** Does not strictly reward earning tough wins over weak schedules.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Retrospective Systems (Our Engine)
- **Objective:** What did teams mathematically earn given what transpired?
- **Standard of Proof:** End-of-season opponent performance back-calculated.
- **Integrity:** Pure game outcomes (W/L/OT) balanced with per-play dominance (EPA).
:::
:::

---

## Graph Disconnection & The FCS Silo

* CFB competition forms a **directed multi-graph** $\mathcal{G} = (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E})$.
* Across 134 FBS teams and 128 FCS teams:
  * Only ~110 cross-division matchups occur annually.
  * Connectivity is sparse and one-sided (FBS hosts ~98% of matchups).
* **Failure of flat priors:**
  * Top FCS teams can inflate via internal transitive cycles without proper regularization.
* **Our Solution:** Hierarchical Bayesian shrinkage.

---

## Pipeline 1: WLD Ordered Logit Resume

We map discrete game outcomes $Y_k \in \{1: \text{L}, 2: \text{OTL}, 3: \text{OTW}, 4: \text{W}\}$:

$$Y_k \sim \text{OrderedLogit}(\eta_k, \mathbf{c})$$

$$\eta_k = \theta_{\text{home}[k]} - \theta_{\text{away}[k]} + \gamma_{\text{home}} \cdot (1 - \text{neutral}_k)$$

* $\theta_i$: Latent resume strength of team $i$.
* $\gamma_{\text{home}} \sim \mathcal{N}(0.2, 0.1^2)$: Home field advantage log-odds.
* $\mathbf{c} = (c_1, c_2, c_3)$: Internal thresholds with $c_1 < c_2 < c_3$.

---

## Pipeline 2: XPD Student-$t$ Efficiency

Net Expected Points Added (EPA) aggregated across all offensive plays:

$$\text{XPD}_k = \sum_{p \in \text{Plays}(k)} \text{EPA}_{p, \text{home}} - \sum_{p \in \text{Plays}(k)} \text{EPA}_{p, \text{away}}$$

Robust Student-$t$ regression protects against 70-point blowouts and garbage time:

$$\text{XPD}_k \sim \text{Student-}t\left(\nu, \, \alpha_{\text{home}[k]} - \alpha_{\text{away}[k]} + \beta_{\text{home}} \cdot (1 - \text{neutral}_k), \, \tau^2\right)$$

* $\alpha_i$: Latent per-play efficiency rating.
* $\nu \sim \text{Gamma}(2, 0.1)$: Heavy-tailed degree of freedom ($\nu \in [4, 8]$).

---

## Hierarchical FCS Regularization

To connect the sparse graph without arbitrary penalty downweighting:

$$\theta_i \sim \mathcal{N}\left(\mu_{\text{sub}[i]}, \, \sigma^2_{\text{sub}[i]}\right)$$

$$\mu_{\text{FBS}} = 0 \quad (\text{Identifiability Anchor})$$

$$\mu_{\text{FCS}} \sim \mathcal{N}(-1.5, 0.5^2) \quad [\text{or } \xi_{\text{FCS}} \sim \mathcal{N}(-21.0, 3.0^2) \text{ in XPD}]$$

* **Elite FCS Programs:** (e.g. North Dakota State) shrink toward upper tail of $\mathcal{N}(\mu_{\text{FCS}}, \sigma^2_{\text{FCS}})$.
* **Weak FCS Programs:** Yield negligible resume equity in $\theta$ and cap XPD gains.

---

## Sonneborn-Berger & Buchholz Metrics

Map posterior opponent strength into game equity: $\mathcal{M}(\theta_j) = \text{logit}^{-1}(\theta_j)$

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Sonneborn-Berger (SB)
$$\text{SB}_i = \sum_{k \in \text{Games}(i)} w_{k, i} \cdot \mathcal{M}(\theta_{\text{opp}[k]})$$
* Outcome weight $w_{k, i} \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$.
* Directly rewards defeating high-quality opponents.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Buchholz (BH / SOS)
$$\text{BH}_i = \sum_{k \in \text{Games}(i)} \mathcal{M}(\theta_{\text{opp}[k]})$$
* Sum of total schedule difficulty faced.
:::
:::

## High-Dimensional Bradley-Terry Insights

Recent theoretical advances formalize non-asymptotic behavior on sparse graphs:

> **Fang, Han, Luo, & Xu (2026)**, *Recent advances in the Bradley–Terry Model: theory, algorithms, and applications*, arXiv:2601.14727.

* Establishes convergence rates under irregular comparison topologies ($p \ll n$).
* Verifies that hierarchical Gaussian shrinkage enforces spectral gap stability.
* Confirms uniform consistency over dynamic ranges when anchor sets are identifiability-constrained.

## Production Pipeline: `targets` + DuckDB

```
[ cfbfastR / CFBD API ]
          │
          ▼
   [ data/cfb.duckdb ]  ◄── Incremental Sync (Weekly)
          │
    targets Graph
    ├── 1. raw_schedules_pbp
    ├── 2. transform_wld_xpd
    ├── 3. fit_wld_stan (cmdstanr)
    ├── 4. fit_xpd_stan (cmdstanr)
    ├── 5. convergence_diagnostics (R-hat <= 1.01, ESS >= 400)
    ├── 6. prior_sensitivity_sweep (Spearman rho >= 0.985)
    ├── 7. benchmark_comparison (AP, CFP, Colley Matrix)
    └── 8. render_reports_and_dashboards
```

---

## Diagnostic Gates & Quality Control

Target pipeline halts if MCMC convergence fails:

| Diagnostic Metric | Strict Threshold | Justification |
|:---|:---:|:---|
| **Max $\widehat{R}$** | $\le 1.01$ | Chains have thoroughly mixed |
| **Min $\text{ESS}_{\text{bulk}}$** | $\ge 400$ | Stable posterior mean & median |
| **Min $\text{ESS}_{\text{tail}}$** | $\ge 400$ | Accurate tail credible intervals |
| **Post-warmup Divergences** | $= 0$ | No geometric funnel traps |
| **Prior Sensitivity $\rho$** | $\ge 0.985$ | Robust to FCS hyperparameter shift |

---

## Conclusion & Q&A

* Dual-pipeline architecture cleanly separates **resume accomplishment** from **play efficiency**.
* Non-centered hierarchical modeling enables robust estimation across 260+ teams.
* Complete reproducibility managed by `targets` and DuckDB.

**Thank you!**
